source: SELECT (Lincoff et al., N Engl J Med 2023): semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction and non-fatal stroke, hazard ratio 0.80 (95% CI 0.72-0.90) over a mean 39.8-month follow-up in 17,604 adults with overweight or obesity and established cardiovascular disease, without diabetes. The relative reduction and its bounds are 1 minus the hazard ratio and its confidence limits. Applied outside that enrolled population it is a transport assumption, which is why `observed_in_subgroup` records where it was actually measured.

SELECT's prespecified analysis of progression to type 2 diabetes among participants with prediabetes at baseline reported a large reduction on semaglutide 2.4 mg. Tier B rather than A because the figure is from a secondary endpoint in a prediabetes subpopulation, and this model applies it to the broader non-diabetic obese population — a transport assumption the trial itself does not make.

SURMOUNT-1's three-year extension in adults with obesity and prediabetes reported a very large reduction in progression to type 2 diabetes on tirzepatide against placebo. Held at 0.90 rather than the headline figure and tiered B, because the enrolled population was prediabetic by design and this model applies the reduction to the wider non-diabetic obese population.

SCALE Obesity and Prediabetes (le Roux et al., Lancet 2017): 2% of the liraglutide 3.0 mg arm developed type 2 diabetes over 160 weeks against 6% on placebo. Tier B for the same transport reason as the other two — the enrolled population was prediabetic.
